top_choice_rationale: P001 honours one identifiable invention, the optical lattice clock with many neutral atoms interrogated at a magic wavelength (Katori), and its development to the 10^-18 regime (Ye). It is mature, independently reproduced in several laboratories, already used for millimetre-scale redshift tests and constraints on varying constants, and was not covered by the 2005 comb prize. The two-name allocation is tight, though priority and the wider clock community remain a caveat, so the citation must stay on the lattice-clock architecture. P002 is a close second: the flat-band prediction and the 2018 correlated and superconducting states are a major new field, but the experimental credit (Dean, Young, Yacoby, Efetov, Yazdani are outside the three names), the narrower theory credit and an open pairing mechanism make it less clean this year. Any award is preferable to none.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; his Chalmers and WACQT colleagues are not among the proposed laureates, though his field of superconducting quantum circuits is adjacent to neither proposal
